name: Whangārei
note: City: Northland's only city and main base, with the Town Basin, Parihaka and Hundertwasser Art Centre.

name: Dargaville
note: Town: Kaipara District's main town, base for the Kauri Coast museums and Baylys Beach.

name: Kaitaia
note: Town: Far North hub and base for Ninety Mile Beach and Cape Reinga tours; Te Ahu Museum is here.

name: Kerikeri
note: Town: Bay of Islands orchard town with the Stone Store mission site, Rainbow Falls and an art and craft trail.

name: Paihia
note: Town: main Bay of Islands tourist base, with cruises, dive operators and the Waitangi Treaty Grounds next door.

name: Russell
note: Town: historic waterfront village across the bay from Paihia, first European settlement in New Zealand (Kororāreka).

name: Opua
note: Village: marina and car ferry terminal to Russell, start of the Twin Coast Cycle Trail.

name: Kawakawa
note: Town: gateway to the Bay of Islands, home of the Hundertwasser public toilets and a tourist train.

name: Rawene
note: Village: historic harbourside village on the Hokianga, with Clendon House and a ferry across the harbour.

name: Opononi
note: Village: Hokianga Harbour village opposite the sand dunes, with Opo the dolphin statue and the Footprints of Kupe show.

name: Whangaroa
note: Village/harbour district: north of the Bay of Islands, Whangaroa Harbour and its beaches (Wikivoyage: "Whangaroa").

name: Mangōnui
note: Village: colonial fishing village on Doubtless Bay with a waterfront heritage trail and fish shop.

name: Coopers Beach
note: Beach village: long surf and swimming beach on Doubtless Bay, near Rangikapiti Pa.

name: Taipa
note: Village: beach settlement on Doubtless Bay, one of the Doubtless Bay coastal towns.

name: Cable Bay
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) Cable Bay Block Road (Taipa-Mangōnui); point approximate
note: Village: Doubtless Bay settlement whose store has a giant ice cream sign, a roadside icon named by the tourism board.

name: Ahipara
note: Village: southern end of Ninety Mile Beach (Wikivoyage: "southern end ... at Ahipara") and horse-trek base.

name: Omapere
note: Village: Hokianga settlement and pier on the road into Waipoua Forest; base for the Footprints Waipoua tour.

name: Kohukohu
note: Village: small Hokianga village with the Village Arts Gallery and the access road to the north-head dunes.

name: Mangamuka Bridge
note: Village: junction on SH1 and starting point of the Omahuta Kauri Sanctuary road (Wikivoyage Hokianga itinerary).

name: Whangārei Heads
note: Area: peninsula of bays, coves and walks (Wikivoyage: "many opportunities for walkers" at Whangarei Heads).

name: Tutukaka
note: Village: harbour base for Poor Knights dive trips and Tutukaka Head tracks.

name: Ngunguru
note: Village: estuary village on the Whangārei coast; Wikivoyage recommends its café and beaches.

name: Matapouri
note: Beach village: Matapouri and nearby Sandy Bay, popular swimming beaches north of Whangārei.

name: Waipu
note: Town: Scottish-settled town near Waipu Caves and the Waipu Scottish Migration Museum.

name: Mangawhai
note: Town: Kaipara coast beach town with the Mangawhai Cliffs walkway.

name: Whananaki
note: Village: coastal settlement and Otamure Bay campsite and track.

name: Whatuwhiwhi
note: Village: beach settlement on the Karikari Peninsula framing Tokerau Beach.

name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
note: Historic site: where the Treaty of Waitangi was signed in 1840; Treaty House, a carved meeting house and war canoe, with paid entry and a visitor centre.

name: Ngā Toki Matawhaorua
note: Landmark: the great waka (war canoe) at Waitangi Treaty Grounds; sits inside the Treaty Grounds site.

name: Pompallier Mission
note: Museum: oldest industrial building in New Zealand, a French Catholic mission print works on The Strand (paid, guided).

name: Russell Museum
note: Museum: two-room local history museum in Russell.

name: Christ Church, Russell
note: Church: oldest surviving church in New Zealand, with musket-ball holes from the 1845 battle; exterior and churchyard visit.

name: Flagstaff Hill
note: Viewpoint: Maiki Hill above Russell, with the Te Maiki flagstaff and a track from town (DOC Flagstaff Hill Track).

name: Long Beach, Russell
note: Beach: forest walk from Russell to the swimming beach over the hill (Wikivoyage: swimming is better at Long Beach).

name: Okiato
note: Historic reserve: site of New Zealand's first capital, reached by the car ferry from Opua.

name: Kororipō Pā
note: Historic site: fortified pā at the head of Kerikeri Inlet, linked to Hongi Hika; short walk from the Stone Store.

name: Rangihoua Heritage Park
note: Historic park: site of the first mission station in Rangihoua Bay (DOC heritage park).

name: Marsden Cross
coordinates_source: approximate: Rangihoua Heritage Park point (Marsden Cross is on the park walk); to verify
note: Historic site: cross marking the first Christian service in New Zealand, on the Rangihoua Bay walk.

name: Battle of Ruapekapeka
note: Historic site: 1846 pā battle site with earthworks and a short track (DOC Ruapekapeka Pā track).

name: Stone Store
note: Historic building: oldest stone building in New Zealand (1832), part of the Kerikeri Mission Station; paid entry.

name: Kemp House
note: Historic building: oldest building in New Zealand (1821-22), visited by guided tour from the Stone Store; part of the Kerikeri Mission Station.

name: St James Church, Kerikeri
note: Church: wooden church above the Stone Store, begun in 1829; a building seen from outside.

name: Rewa's Village
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Kerikeri listing (opposite the Stone Store)
note: Museum: replica Māori kainga (fishing village) opposite the Stone Store, with a marae and canoes.

name: Rainbow Falls
note: Waterfall: 27 m falls on the Kerikeri River, reached by car park or a 4 km walk from the Stone Store.

name: Kerikeri Fairy Pools
note: Natural pools: swimming pools on the Kerikeri River, reached by track from St James Church or the youth hostel.

name: Wharepōke Subtropical Garden
note: Garden: 2 ha subtropical garden about 1 km from Kerikeri, listed as a garden of regional significance.

name: Makana Chocolate Factory
note: Shop: chocolate factory and outlet on Kerikeri Road (factory shop).

name: Kerikeri Farmers Market
note: Market: Sunday-morning farmers market in Kerikeri (weekly, not a permanent venue).

name: Mangōnui Craft Market
note: Market: Saturday craft market at the Mangōnui Hall (weekly, not a permanent venue).

name: Rangikapiti Pā
note: Historic site: former Māori pā with views over Doubtless Bay, near Coopers Beach.

name: Taumarumaru Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: three former pā sites with walking tracks, reached from the highway or Coopers Beach sand.

name: Butler Point Whaling Museum
note: Museum: restored 1847 homestead, gardens and museum at Hihi; open by appointment (Wikivoyage).

name: Matthews Vintage Collection
note: Museum: vintage cars, tractors and engines on State Highway 10.

name: Mangōnui Heritage Trail
note: Walk: 3 km walk around Mangōnui's historic sites, starting from the Doubtless Bay Information Centre.

name: Matauri Bay
note: Beach: family swimming bay with views of the Cavalli Islands, north of Kerikeri.

name: Cavalli Islands
note: Islands: group of islands off Matauri Bay, seen from the bay and tours.

name: Tauranga Bay
note: Beach: picturesque white sand beach in the Whangaroa district with a family campground.

name: Taupō Bay
note: Beach: white sand bay in the Whangaroa district with a family campground.

name: Tokerau Beach
note: Beach: 18 km surf beach on the Karikari Peninsula, named by the tourism board.

name: Maitai Bay
note: Beach: sheltered bay at the tip of the Karikari Peninsula with a headland track and campsite.

name: Rarawa Beach
note: Beach: long beach with a coastal walk on the Aupōuri-side Wharekāpu–Paxton Point area.

name: Karikari Peninsula
note: Peninsula: beaches, golf and the Lake Ōhia link to the mainland; DOC Karikari Peninsula reserves.

name: Doubtless Bay
note: Bay: large bay with beaches and villages (Mangōnui, Coopers Beach, Taipa, Cable Bay).

name: Cape Reinga Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: 1941 lighthouse at Te Rerenga Wairua, the northern tip of the North Island; the walk and viewpoint are the visit.

name: Cape Reinga / Te Rerenga Wairua
note: Headland: northernmost accessible point of mainland New Zealand, where the Tasman and Pacific oceans meet; sacred to Māori.

name: Te Paki Sand Dunes
note: Natural landmark: giant sand dunes at the north end of Ninety Mile Beach; sandboarding and walks.

name: Te Paki Coastal Track
note: Walk: coastal track in Te Paki Recreation Reserve from the Te Paki Stream towards Cape Reinga.

name: Ara Pou Pou Trail
note: Walk: pou-marked cultural trail in Te Paki Recreation Reserve.

name: Spirits Bay
note: Beach: remote bay in the Te Paki area, reached by 4WD track with a campsite (Kapowairua).

name: Ninety Mile Beach
other_sources: https://www.openstreetmap.org (wiki: Te Oneroa-a-Tōhē / Ninety Mile Beach)
note: Beach: 88 km beach used as a road, reached from Ahipara, Kaitaia and coach tours; not part of Cape Reinga.

name: Te Kōhanga Shipwreck Bay
note: Beach: southern end of Te Oneroa-a-Tōhē, named as the start of the Te Hiku journey.

name: Ripirō Beach
note: Beach: 26 km Kaipara-coast surf beach near Dargaville and Baylys Beach.

name: Baylys Beach
note: Beach: surf beach 12 km west of Dargaville.

name: Uretiti Beach
note: Beach: surf and camping beach near Waipu with a DOC campsite.

name: Bream Bay
note: Bay: long bay between Ruakākā and Waipu with beaches and surf; no visitor source names a specific stop.

name: Onerahi Beach
note: Beach: closest swimming beach to Whangārei, with a playground.

name: Ocean Beach, Whangārei
note: Beach: big white sand surf beach about 36 km from Whangārei town centre.

name: Bream Head
note: Headland: scenic reserve and historic site at the Whangārei Heads, with walks and coastal views.

name: Mount Manaia
note: Viewpoint: 403 m peak in the Whangārei Heads with a track to the summit and sweeping views (DOC Mount Manaia Track).

name: Smugglers Bay
note: Beach: bay at the Whangārei Heads, reached by loop track (DOC Smugglers Bay Loop Track).

name: Peach Cove
note: Beach: cove at the Whangārei Heads, reached by a DOC track.

name: Motukiore Island
note: Island: island walk off the Whangārei Heads (DOC Motukiore Island Walk).

name: Hundertwasser Toilets
note: Landmark: Hundertwasser-designed public toilets in Kawakawa, a famous roadside stop.

name: Kawakawa Bay of Islands Vintage Railway
note: Railway: heritage tourist train on a 19th-century line through Kawakawa; a ride is the attraction.

name: Ngāwhā Springs
note: Hot springs: geothermal pools near Ōkaihau, a paid spa and pool complex.

name: Opua Forest Paihia Lookout Track
note: Walk: one-hour return walk from School Road to the Paihia lookout over the bay and Russell.

name: Cape Brett Track
note: Walk: 16.3 km track to Cape Brett lighthouse and hut, reached by water taxi or from Oke Bay; a multi-day trip.

name: Cape Brett Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: 1909 lighthouse at the end of the Cape Brett track, reached on foot or by boat.

name: Hole in the Rock
note: Natural arch: Hole in the Rock on Piercy Island, seen on the Bay of Islands cruise (the rock is the spot; cruises are how you reach it).

name: Urupukapuka Island
note: Island: largest island in the Bay of Islands, reserve with walks, bays and campsites, visited on boat trips.

name: Moturua Island
note: Island: scenic reserve in the Bay of Islands with a DOC island track.

name: Motuarohia (Roberton Island)
note: Island: recreation reserve in the Bay of Islands with a Roberton Island track.

name: Motukawanui Island
note: Island: scenic reserve in the Bay of Islands with a hut and island track.

name: Pataua Island
note: Island: recreation reserve island near Whangārei with a short island track.

name: Whangamumu Whaling Station
note: Historic site: ruins of a whaling station on Whangamumu Harbour, reached by walk from Whangamumu.

name: Poor Knights Islands
note: Islands: marine reserve and nature reserve, a world-famous dive site reached by boat from Tutukaka; landing not allowed.

name: Hen and Chicken Islands
note: Islands: nature reserve off Whangārei, seen from boats and dive charters.

name: Whangārei Harbour Marine Reserve
note: Harbour: marine reserve and harbour in Whangārei, with boat and kayak trips.

name: Whangaruru North Head
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) Puriri Bay (Whangaruru North Head) campsite; visitor point
note: Headland: scenic reserve with a track to the north head and Puriri Bay campsite.

name: Mimiwhangata Coastal Park
note: Park: coastal park with beaches, dunes, a marine park and a peninsula loop walk, about an hour from Whangārei.

name: Whangārei Falls
note: Waterfall: 25 m waterfall in a bush-fringed pool, 5 km north-east of the city.

name: Whangārei Quarry Gardens
note: Garden: terraced subtropical garden in a quarry with waterfalls and a lake, with a café.

name: Hundertwasser Art Centre
note: Museum: art centre designed by Friedensreich Hundertwasser in the Town Basin, with a Māori art gallery; paid entry.

name: Claphams National Clock Museum
note: Museum: one of the largest clock collections in the southern hemisphere, at the Town Basin; paid.

name: Kiwi North
note: Museum: Whangārei Museum, kiwi aviary and heritage park at Maunu; paid.

name: Mount Parihaka
note: Viewpoint: 1 Parihaka reserve over Whangārei with a track and paved road to the summit and war memorial; glow-worms at night (Wikivoyage: Mair Park and Parihaka Reserve). Wikipedia title only redirects to Whangārei, so 0 views.

name: Whangārei Town Basin
note: Waterfront: restored town basin with museums, galleries and cafés on the Hātea River.

name: AE Fun Park
note: Activity park: paintball, laser tag, flying fox and mini golf at Maungakaramea, 15 min south of Whangārei.

name: Whangārei Aquatic Centre
note: Pool: public aquatic centre with a wave pool and hydroslides (civic leisure facility).

name: Waro Limestone Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: limestone scenic reserve near Whangārei with a short walk.

name: Waipū Caves
note: Cave: limestone caves near Waipu, reached by a DOC track.

name: Mangawhai Cliffs Walkway
note: Walk: cliff-top walkway over the Mangawhai coast.

name: Waiotemarama Falls
note: Waterfall: bush track to falls, about 5 km from Opononi.

name: Tangihua Forest
note: Forest: Tangihua Forest with several tracks and a hut, in the Northland ranges.

name: Tokatoka Scenic Reserve
note: Reserve: scenic reserve with a summit track near Dargaville.

name: Mount Tutamoe
note: Peak: summit of the Tutamoe range inland from Dargaville, reached by a DOC track.

name: Kai Iwi Lakes
note: Lakes: three dune lakes in a reserve 32 km north of Dargaville, for swimming and walks.

name: Kumara Box
note: Attraction: kumara-themed show and an oil-drum train ride with marine collection, booking essential.

name: Kauri Museum
note: Museum: large kauri timber and kauri gum museum in Matakohe, paid; the standalone spot kauri-museum already in the app.

name: Dargaville Museum
note: Museum: maritime and local history museum in Dargaville, paid.

name: Kaipara Vintage Machinery Museum
note: Museum: vintage machinery at Harding Park, next to the Dargaville Museum.

name: Woodturners Kauri Gallery
note: Shop: kauri woodturning studio and gallery on SH12 in Dargaville (a shop with a studio).

name: Matakohe Post Office
note: Heritage building: historic post office in Matakohe, seen from the road.

name: Kohukohu Village Arts Gallery
note: Gallery: Hokianga community art gallery on Kohukohu's main street (a gallery with exhibitions).

name: Hokianga Sand Dunes
note: Natural landmark: sand dunes across the Hokianga Harbour from Opononi, reached by the Hokianga Express ferry and a climb of about 2.5 km; the north-head dunes are reached from Mitimiti.

name: Opo the Dolphin Statue
note: Statue: statue of Opo the dolphin at Opononi's pier, a roadside photo stop.

name: Footprints of Kupe (Manea)
note: Attraction: 75-minute Māori cultural presentation with performance, film and digital interaction; paid.

name: Clendon House
note: Historic house: 1869 house of Captain James Clendon in Rawene, open limited days.

name: Rawene Mangrove Boardwalk
note: Boardwalk: short boardwalk through mangroves at Rawene's Clendon Esplanade.

name: Māngungu Mission
note: Historic house: Mangungu Mission House at Horeke, one of the five Historic Places Trust sites in Hokianga.

name: Te Waimate Mission
note: Historic site: 1831 mission station near Waimate North with a church and mission buildings.

name: Koutu Boulders
note: Natural landmark: large concretions in Koutu, Hokianga, billed as the biggest in the world; a short walk.

name: Wairere Boulders
note: Natural landmark: basalt flow boulders near Horeke, a world-unique natural formation.

name: Puketī and Ōmahuta Forests
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) Puketī Forest (natural/wood); forest is large, point is the forest centre
note: Forest: 21,000 ha forest with kauri, kōkako and kiwi, walks and camping; includes Omahuta Kauri Sanctuary.

name: Manginangina Kauri Walk
note: Walk: kauri walk in Puketi Forest, the dawn chorus site.

name: Trounson Kauri Park
note: Park: 586 ha mainland island with kauri stands, kiwi and a loop track, 40 km north of Dargaville.

name: Waipoua Forest
note: Forest: largest remaining native forest tract in Northland, home of the giant kauri on SH12.

name: Tāne Mahuta
note: Tree: largest living kauri, 200 m walk from the car park on SH12.

name: Te Matua Ngahere
note: Tree: second-largest kauri, "Father of the Forest", reached by a walk from the car park.

name: Waipoua Forest Scenic Lookout
note: Viewpoint: hilltop lookout over Waipoua Forest, reached by Lookout Road from SH12.

name: Omahuta Kauri Sanctuary
note: Forest: ecologically undisturbed kauri forest near Mangamuka Bridge; part of the Puketī and Ōmahuta forests.

name: Herekino Forest
note: Forest: forest with the Kaitaia Walkway near Kaitaia.

name: Lake Ngatu
note: Lake: recreation reserve lake with a track around it (DOC Lake Ngatu Track).

name: Lake Ōmāpere
note: Lake: lake next to Omapere, used for swimming and boating.

name: Te Ahu Museum
note: Museum: Far North regional museum in Kaitaia, admission by donation.

name: Gumdiggers Park
note: Museum: kauri gum and kauri industry museum on a historic gum digging site at Awanui, paid.

name: Sir Hek Busby Kupe Waka Centre
note: Cultural centre: waka and Kupe centre named in the Top of the North; location not yet checked.

name: Whangaroa Museum
note: Museum: small local museum in Kaeo, open Monday to Friday.

name: Taratara Rock
note: Rock: climbable rock beside State Highway 10 in the Whangaroa district.

name: Duke's Nose (Kaiaraara Rock)
note: Viewpoint: rock formation and hike above Whangaroa Harbour (DOC Dukes Nose Kairaara Rocks Track).

name: St Paul's Rock
note: Viewpoint: rock summit with a track above Whangaroa Harbour.

name: Mahinepua Peninsula
note: Peninsula: beaches and walk on the Whangaroa Harbour coast (DOC Mahinepua Peninsula Track).

name: Whangaroa Harbour
note: Harbour: sheltered harbour with beaches, walks and kayaking north of the Bay of Islands.

name: Watkin Powell Track (Otamure Bay)
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) Otamure Bay (Whananaki) Campsite; trailhead point
note: Walk: coastal track from Whananaki to Otamure Bay.

name: Tutukaka Head Tracks
note: Walk: coastal tracks at Tutukaka Head above the dive harbour.

name: Martins Bay Track
note: Walk: coastal track at the Hokianga Heads.

name: Lake Ōhia
note: Lake: lake at the Karikari Peninsula neck named by the tourism board.

name: Kermadec Islands
note: Islands: remote subtropical islands with restricted access (DOC visits by permit only); not a visitor destination.

name: Russell Forest and Ngaiotonga Scenic Reserve
note: Forest: scenic reserve with tracks above Russell (DOC Nancy Fladgate track).

name: Waewaetorea Island
note: Island: recreation reserve island in the Bay of Islands.
